MSFC-9906958.sy: This Quick Time movie demonstrates the Magnetic Launch Assist system, previously referred to as the Magnetic Levitation (Maglev) system, for space launch using a 5 foot model of a reusable Bantam Class launch vehicle on a 50 foot track that provided 6-g acceleration and 6-g de-acceleration. Overcoming the grip of Earth?s gravity is a supreme challenge for engineers who design rockets that leave the planet. Engineers at the Marshall Space Flight Center have developed and tested Magnetic Launch Assist technologies that could levitate and accelerate a launch vehicle along a track at high speeds before it leaves the ground. Using electricity and magnetic fields, a Magnetic Launch Assist system would drive a spacecraft along a horizontal track until it reaches desired speeds. A full-scale, operational track would be about 1.5-miles long and capable of accelerating a vehicle to 600 mph in 9.5 seconds. The major advantages of launch assist for NASA launch vehicles is that it reduces the weight of the takeoff, the landing gear, the wing size, and less propellant resulting in significant cost savings. The film and the campaign itself were intended to undermine the long-haul trucking industry in the eyes of the public, by making the point that tractor trailer trucks do not pay their fair share of highway construction and maintenance costs. "Highways and Byways" was in fact entered into evidence in a 1957 antitrust case brought by interstate long-haul truckers and the Pennsylvania Motor Truck Association against the the Eastern Railroad Presidents Conference. In the end, the Supreme Court unanimously ruled that the railroads' publicity campaign was protected by the First Amendment, and dismissed the trucking industries' claims.
